query_text: Need a web app for brand superfans where they can get into a special members-only area and see new stuff before anyone else does, like early looks at upcoming products, behind-the-scenes posts, and exclusive videos, with a clean home screen that shows all the fresh content in one place and a little badge or counter so fans know how many new things they haven't checked out yet.

After-sales ticket manager for a browser-based tool where customers can submit a problem, pick a category like broken item or wrong delivery, and our support team can see all open cases on one side with the details on the other, so nobody has to chase each other by email anymore and every ticket shows its current status and who's handling it.

Make a vendor onboarding web app that walks new suppliers through every step they need to finish before they're approved to work with us, with a checklist of required documents and compliance items they need to tick off, and a status tracker on our side so we can see at a glance who's done what and who's still missing stuff.

Build a browser-based expense report tool where employees can fill in what they spent, attach a photo of the receipt, and submit it for approval, and their manager gets a list of pending requests they can approve or send back with a note, so the whole reimbursement process stops living in email threads and everyone can see where their claim is sitting.

Contract manager web app for handling the whole life of a business agreement, from drafting and sharing it with the other company, to both sides signing it online, to getting a reminder when it's about to expire, with a list of all active and past contracts on the left and the full details plus signing area on the right side of the screen.

IT equipment tracker for a website where staff can look up every laptop, monitor, and phone the company owns, see who each one is assigned to, and submit a request if they need something new or need a repair, so the IT team stops getting requests on chat and has one place to manage all the hardware and pending asks.

Make a brand file library web app where the marketing team can upload and find all the official logos, color guides, fonts, and photos in one place, with folders organized by type and a search bar so people stop asking where the latest version of the logo is, and each file shows the upload date so everyone grabs the newest one.

Create a web app where managers can run quarterly reviews for their team, fill in scores and comments for each person, and set goals they want them to hit by next quarter, with a summary showing how each employee is tracking against their targets so review season stops being a pile of random spreadsheets sent back and forth.

Build a purchase request tool for desktop browsers where anyone at the company can fill in what they need to buy, attach a quote, and send it up the chain for sign-off, with a list showing all pending requests and their approval status, so procurement stops happening over chat messages and everything has a clear paper trail.

Need a supplier rating web app where our team can score each vendor on things like delivery speed, product quality, and communication, save those scores in one place, and pull up a ranked list anytime we need to decide who to work with next, with a profile page for each supplier that shows all their past ratings and whether they're currently qualified.

Create a carbon footprint calculator and reporting tool for a web app where we input our company's energy use, travel, and shipping numbers each month, and it turns that into a running total of our emissions so we can actually put real figures in our sustainability reports, with a chart showing how we're trending over time.

Create a compliance training tracker for a web app where HR can see which employees have finished their required courses and certifications, with a list of who's overdue on the left and the details of each person's completed and pending training on the right, plus automatic reminders that go out when a cert is about to expire so nobody misses a deadline.

Create a sales territory planner web app where sales managers can divide up regions among the team, assign a revenue target to each rep, and track how close everyone is to hitting their number for the quarter, with a simple table showing each territory, the rep responsible, and their progress so quota conversations have actual data behind them.

Create a new employee onboarding tracker as a web app where HR and the new hire can both see a checklist of everything that needs to happen in the first few weeks, like signing documents, finishing training, and meeting key people, with a progress bar so everyone knows how far along the setup is and nothing important slips through the cracks.

Create a software license tracker as a browser-based tool where we can log every subscription and tool the company pays for, note when each one renews, and see a list sorted by upcoming renewal date so we stop finding out a license expired after the fact, with a spot to record the cost and the number of seats so we can audit what we actually use.

Make a website that works as a proper manifesto and about page rolled into one, the kind that feels like someone actually wrote it and means it, with a bold opening statement that sets the tone, a short story about why this company exists, and a list of the things we stand for, all laid out in a way that feels considered and a little different from the usual corporate template.

Build a product launch site for a web app that has real personality, where each key feature gets its own moment as you scroll down, with small animations that bring the demo to life instead of just being a wall of screenshots, and the whole thing should feel sharp and confident, the kind of site that makes someone want to sign up just from the vibe.

Make a product demo website where visitors can actually try the thing in a live preview area right there in the browser, not just watch a video, with a sidebar that shows what each part of the product does as you click around, so the site has a real identity and feels like a proper playground rather than a boring walkthrough.

A startup pitch website that tells the investor story as a proper journey from top to bottom, where each scroll step reveals the next chapter, from the problem, to our solution, to the numbers, to the team, so it feels like reading something worth your time rather than flipping through a deck someone converted to a PDF and uploaded.

Create a press kit website that has genuine style, where journalists and partners can find the company story, download logos in every format they need, and grab high-res photos without having to email anyone, with everything cleanly organized so it feels like a real brand put it together, not an afterthought thrown up before a launch.

A public roadmap site that actually has a point of view, showing what we've shipped, what's coming next, and what we're thinking about down the line, all on a timeline that feels alive and worth bookmarking, with a spot where users can leave a comment on upcoming features so it feels like a real conversation rather than a one-way announcement board.

Create a customer stories website that has the warmth of real testimonials, where each case study gets its own page with the background, the specific problem, and the outcome in the customer's own words, and the main listing area feels curated rather than dumped, so visitors browsing on desktop can filter by industry and actually find stories that resonate with them.

Need a website that serves as an integrations and partners directory with real character, where people can browse all the tools and services that connect to our platform, filter by category, and click through to a page for each one that explains what it does and how it connects, so the whole thing feels like a living ecosystem rather than a plain list on a forgotten corner of the site.

Build a company culture website that actually shows who we are, with real team photos, short bios that sound like people wrote them, and the values laid out in a way that feels earned rather than copied from a template, all inside a web app that has a distinct visual identity so when someone opens it in their browser they immediately get a sense of what this place is actually like.

Need a pricing page site that has conviction, where each plan is laid out side by side with a clear comparison of what you get at each tier, and the whole thing is honest enough that you can actually make a decision without having to contact sales, designed for desktop browsers with a layout that feels considered and reflects a brand that knows what it's offering.
